title: Couple a tractor's air line to the trailer's gladhand: off the dummy coupler, seals together at 90 degrees, turn to lock
instruction: Connect the tractor's air line to the trailer, then let go.
context: Heavy and Tractor-Trailer Truck Drivers (O*NET 53-3032.00, about 2.2 million employed) connect the air lines at every trailer hookup. O*NET lists the task: "Couple or uncouple trailers by changing trailer jack positions, connecting or disconnecting air or electrical lines, or manipulating fifth-wheel locks." (https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/53-3032.00) Driver's manuals describe the move: press the two seals together with the couplers at 90 degrees, then turn the hose's glad hand to lock, red (emergency) to red; unused hoses are stored on dummy couplers. It is a rotary lock under load: the full-size 0.45 kg coupler hangs on a hose that pulls on it throughout, mates face to face on a horizontal axis, and locks only if the seals stay squeezed while its lug rides under the other coupler's flange. Turned with the seals apart it doesn't engage; stopped short it blows apart under pressure.
setup: YAM station (scene=station), both arms at their ready pose. World frame: origin between the arm bases, x forward, y to the left, z up; heights are above the table top. Trailer nose plate: grey-painted steel plate, 40 cm wide (y) x 32 cm tall x 5 mm thick, standing upright across the table with its front face at x 0.45 m, centred at y 0, fixed. Two trailer gladhands on 4 cm brass bulkhead fittings through the plate, fixed, seal faces toward the robot (-x) and bodies pointing up: a red (emergency) gladhand at y +0.10 m and a blue (service) gladhand at y -0.10 m, seal centres 25 cm up. Each gladhand (the two on the plate and the one on the hose) has an aluminium body 150 mm long, 50 mm across the seal face and 30 mm thick at the grip, 0.45 kg, painted red or blue; a cast-iron connector plate with a ramped locking lug on one side and a flange on the other; and a black rubber seal 45 mm across that compresses up to 3 mm. One tractor air line: 1.0 m of red 3/8 in ID rubber air hose, 19 mm OD, 0.25 kg, running from a fixed brass fitting 15 cm up on the outer face of a grey steel post (6 x 6 x 20 cm, fixed, at x 0.10 m, y +0.42 m), leaving it straight ahead (+x), looping out beside the plate and ending in a red gladhand. That gladhand starts locked, seal face down, on a dummy coupler: a gladhand-shaped grey steel block with the same lug and flange, a plain steel face and no air port, standing seal face up on a grey steel bracket (5 x 5 x 9 cm) at x 0.22 m, y +0.30 m, its seal centre 12 cm up; the locked gladhand's body points straight ahead (+x) and comes off with a quarter turn clockwise seen from above. Friction: seals and hose 1.0 static, 0.8 dynamic; lugs, plates and bodies 0.4 static, 0.3 dynamic. One fixed layout (-E object_jitter=0).
scoring: Scored at the end of the trial. The hose's gladhand is locked to a trailer gladhand when all three hold: the two connector plates are no more than 2 mm further apart than when fully locked; it has turned to within 10 degrees of the lock stop (its body pointing down, opposite the trailer gladhand's body); and it stays on when pulled 60 N along its hose for 1 s (in simulation: the locking lug is fully under the flange). 0 if the gladhand is still on its dummy coupler (seal centre within 5 cm of the dummy's). 0.2 if it is off its dummy coupler but not locked. 0.8 if it is locked to the red trailer gladhand. 1.0 if it is locked to the red trailer gladhand and both grippers have been at least 2 cm clear of every gladhand and the hose for the last 1 s. The score is 0 if it ends locked to the blue trailer gladhand, if any part of the gladhand or hose is ever more than 2 cm below the table top (off the table or on the floor), or if the hose's fixed end is ever pulled more than 5 mm from its fitting. Real trial: angle from a photo against the lock stop, plate gap with a feeler gauge, pull with a spring scale.
reset_notes: Turn the hose's gladhand off the trailer gladhand and lock it back onto its dummy coupler, body pointing straight ahead. Lay the hose in a loose loop on the table, running forward from the post and back to the gladhand. Wipe the seals and replace any that is cut or flattened. Real trials are safe to run: the hose carries no air, so there is no pressure hazard, and the 0.45 kg gladhand falls at most 25 cm onto the table.
fidelity: Isaac Sim (PhysX) rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. Real-size gladhands built from convex pieces; the lock comes from contact alone (lug under a ramped flange, detent, stop), nothing scripted. The plate profile is our own parametric model, not measured from an SAE J318 part. Seals: 67 N/mm springs, 3 mm travel, about 97 N when locked. Hose: 20 rigid 5 cm capsules with bending stiffness, softer than real hose. No air flows; the 60 N pull is replaced by checking the lug is under the flange. See README.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 2,400 steps (termination: step limit); scripted demo: 1.0 after 866 steps
